newsitem.title: CANADA: ATHLETICS-SURIN WINS SPRINT AT MONTREAL INDOOR MEET.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-SURIN WINS SPRINT AT MONTREAL INDOOR MEET.

text.p: Bruny Surin blew past early leader Donovan Powell of Jamaica and won by a stride over Olympic relay teammate Robert Esmie in the 60 metres at the Montreal Athletics Grand Prix on Friday.
Surin, the two-time world indoor champion, won in a modest time of 6.60 seconds.
American Vince Henderson was third in 6.68.
"For me, this is a chance to race in Canada ," said Surin. "Especially here in Montreal where I live, it was important to win."
Surin has a greater goal in mind, a third straight world indoor 60 metres title in Paris in March, with $50,000 on the line for the winner.

"That's my goal for the indoor season," said Surin, who teammed with Esmie, Olympic sprint champion Donovan Bailey and Glenroy Gilbert to win gold in the sprint relay last summer at the Atlanta Olympics.

Esmie said he was not disappointed with his time since he is nursing a strained left hamstring. "I'll be ready for the world indoors," he said. "I'll be the only one capable of stopping Bruny from winning three in a row."
In other events, D'Andre Hill of the United States won the women's 60 metres in 7.43 seconds.
Kwaku Boateng, a Ghana native living in Montreal, won the high jump at 2.27 metres.
Boateng was among six Ghanians who left the athletes village at the 1994 Commonwealth Games in Victoria, took a bus to Montreal and applied for refugee status.
They have remained in Montreal ever since and expect to receive landed immigrant status next week. Boateng hopes to represent Canada at the world indoor championships.
